review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for uses of the simp-relevant declarations. The `_coe` lemmas for `mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv` are used only inside this file. `Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/IsManifold/InteriorBoundary.lean` uses only `hf.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv hn`, not the `_coe` lemmas. The other simp attributes (`toFun'_toOpenPartialHomeomorph`, the `simps` calls) look consistent. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether the proposed simp attributes cause any simp-set conflict. They look safe because the rewrites are definitional (`rfl`) and go from a wrapper to the plain `mfderiv`.

findings.excerpt:
lemma Diffeomorph.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv_coe (Φ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    Φ.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv hn x = mfderiv% Φ x := by rfl
findings.problem: The `IsLocalDiffeomorphAt` version of this coercion lemma is tagged `@[simp, mfld_simps]`. The two sibling lemmas, for `Diffeomorph` (L452) and `IsLocalDiffeomorph` (L466), are not. Each of the three wrapper definitions is a separate constant, and the simp lemma for `IsLocalDiffeomorphAt` does not fire on `Diffeomorph.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv Φ hn x` or `IsLocalDiffeomorph.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv hf hn x`, because the head symbols differ. So a goal containing `Φ.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv hn x` or `hf.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv hn x` cannot be normalised to `mfderiv% Φ x` or `mfderiv% f x` by `simp`. The user has to call the lemma by name. The simp normal form is therefore inconsistent across the three variants.
findings.proposed_change: Mark both lemmas like the `IsLocalDiffeomorphAt` one: `@[simp, mfld_simps] lemma Diffeomorph.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv_coe ...` and `@[simp, mfld_simps] lemma IsLocalDiffeomorph.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv_coe ...`. Both are valid rewrite rules. The left side is the wrapper applied to a point. The right side is the plain `mfderiv`, which is simpler and cannot loop. The wrapper does not appear on the right.
findings.benefit: Users who obtain a continuous linear equivalence from a diffeomorphism or a global local diffeomorphism get the same automatic reduction to `mfderiv` as for the pointwise `IsLocalDiffeomorphAt` version. Statements about these differentials then reach a single normal form.

evidence.excerpt: hf.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv hn x = mfderiv% f x :=
